description: We tell the stories of retired space probes to keep their memory alive and spark new inspiration in everyone.
summary:
We built two web experiences that tell the story of Voyager 1 and 2, NASA hardware now drifting through deep space, for school-age space enthusiasts. The first is a kid-friendly site with visual, interactive elements and switchable explanations for kids and adults. The second is a 3D exploration app where users freely explore space, follow each spacecraft’s trajectory, and uncover the events at highlighted points along its journey. Trajectory data comes from NASA/JPL Horizons System, and images are from NASA.

Our approach addresses the challenge by turning the journey of space hardware into an explorable story in plain language, showing where each spacecraft has been, what it saw, and the science it made possible. This matters because complex mission history often fails to hold young learners’ attention. We make it approachable, and guide curious users on to NASA’s original data.
details:
What it does

We built two web experiences that tell the story of Voyager 1 and 2 to school-age learners.

  • Aggregator Site: A visual, interactive overview of the Voyager missions. Users can switch between kid and adult explanations, and follow links to NASA’s official data.
  • Exploration App: A 3D space environment where users freely explore space, follow each spacecraft’s trajectory drawn as a line, and open the story behind each highlighted event point.
How it works
  1. Trajectory data: We downloaded Voyager 1 and 2 trajectory data in advance from NASA/JPL Horizons System via its API, and draw them as lines in 3D space.
  2. Event points: Key events are placed on the trajectory and emphasized by color and size, so users can find them quickly.
  3. Storytelling: Selecting a point shows a short story in plain language, with NASA imagery.
  4. Audience switch: Users toggle between kid and adult explanations at any time.
  5. Path to data: Each story links to the related NASA resource.
Benefits and goals
  • Makes spacecraft history approachable for school-age learners
  • Lets users feel the vastness of space through hands-on exploration
  • Guides curious users from a story to NASA’s original data
Future plans
  • User-contributed events and more immersive design (showing the user’s position as a spacecraft, cockpit-style buttons, background music and sound effects)
  • Upcoming events, such as Voyager 1 reaching one light-day from Earth
  • More spacecraft, such as Galileo and LCROSS
How it is creative

We turn trajectory data into a journey that users walk through themselves, and tell each stop as a story rather than a list of facts.

Factors we considered
  • Plain language that a school-age child can follow
  • Accuracy, through NASA’s official data and images
  • Easy discovery of events, through color, size, and lines
  • A clear route from curiosity to deeper learning
Tools
  • Exploration App: Unity (3D space environment), hosted on Firebase
  • Aggregator Site: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, hosted on GitHub Pages
USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI)

We used Claude and ChatGPT (including Codex) as support tools for consulting on the spacecraft stories and translating our materials into English, discussing the product structure, and coding. We also used an AI image generation tool to create a few illustrations that depict people's reactions to seeing the spacecraft. All photographs of planets and other celestial bodies are NASA's, and none of them were AI-generated. All final decisions were made by our team: we checked the nuance of the detailed wording, judged when the materials were complete, and decided when the product was ready to deploy.
